**THIS IMAGE DEPICTS:** Levin crouches on the gravel and draws a dragon shape with his finger. Bright autumn afternoon sunlight warms the park. The mood is calm and focused.

Generate a SINGLE illustration filling the canvas, bleeding off all four edges — no borders, frames, margins, white edges, panel keylines, split screens, grids, or collages. No lettering on any surface — no words, names or letters anywhere in the image. The only exception: text the Visual Bible explicitly specifies for an element is painted exactly as specified. Bracketed names like `[CharacterA]` and object ids are identifiers only — never painted into the image. Draw exactly one of each named object.

When the FIRST reference photo shows a real location (architecture, landscape, no characters), render the scene IN it — copy its setting, geography and light direction, not its rendering: if it looks photographic, the ART STYLE below still governs. All OTHER reference photos define character IDENTITY only — face, hair, skin tone, build, clothing — never pose, framing, or composition. Each character's position, action, body direction and size come from the scene description and the COMPOSITION rules below.

AGE & PROPORTIONS (render each character at their real age, regardless of the action described):
- Levin: preschool-age proportions about 4.5 heads tall, large head relative to body, soft rounded features, clearly taller than a toddler and smaller than a kindergarten child

**WORN ITEMS ON THIS PAGE (the attached references are not authoritative for these):**
- Levin IS wearing this on this page: red wool cap — a chunky-knit red wool pull-on cap with a folded ribbed cuff. Draw it on Levin even if the attached reference shows Levin without it.
- Levin IS wearing this on this page: green fleece jacket — a forest-green zip-up fleece jacket with a wide body and two front pockets. Draw it on Levin even if the attached reference shows Levin without it.

Levin—a preschool-age boy roughly four-and-a-half heads tall, with wavy short light blonde hair, green eyes, wearing a chunky-knit red wool pull-on cap, a forest-green zip-up fleece jacket, a long-sleeved white cotton shirt, straight-leg dark navy corduroy trousers, and lace-up brown leather ankle boots—crouches in the right foreground facing left, dragging his right index finger through the pale grey gravel of the Lindenhof. Bright afternoon autumn sunlight warms the large linden tree roots rising around him, as he carefully traces the curved shape of a dragon into the small stones. Red and yellow dry leaves are scattered thickly across the ground under his knees and around his boots. The medium shot focuses closely on his focused work, the broad roots forming a quiet, natural barrier behind him.
**REQUIRED OBJECTS IN THIS SCENE (each appears exactly as the scene description places it):**
* **red cap** (clothing) (worn by Levin) — worn on Levin, not a separate free-standing copy
* **green fleece** (clothing) (worn by Levin) — worn on Levin, not a separate free-standing copy
A state that divides, opens or breaks an object does not multiply its markings: a device, emblem or pattern on the surface is one marking, and the split runs through it — each part shows only its share.

**SEASON:** Autumn. Foliage, ground cover, sky and daylight colour are autumn's throughout the book — identical from page to page for the same place, and matching autumn even when a reference photo was taken in another season. Indoor frames and the page's own time of day are unaffected.

**ART STYLE:** A bold, expressive traditional watercolor painting: prominent visible brushstrokes, strong wet-on-wet washes bleeding together, pigment pooling and granulating, rough cold-press paper texture throughout, edges dissolving into the paper. Paint-dominant: no hard outlines, no ink or pencil lines. Characters stay fully opaque, never see-through. Warm, not overly vibrant. Painted by hand, never captured by a camera: no bokeh, no lens flare, no photographic grain, no skin pores, no camera-real fabric; depth from atmospheric haze, not optical blur; visible brushwork on every surface, faces included. No sharp photoreal rendering; a photograph with a painterly filter is still a photograph. Faces: loose washes with visible brushstroke texture. Each character keeps their real age — babies, children, teenagers, adults and grandparents each look it.

**REQUIRED CAST:** Every character named in the reference list is in the frame, exactly one of each, and no one else is added. A character the scene description gives no action to is still drawn, placed where the moment puts them and doing something consistent with it.

**DEPTH AND SIZE:** Depth is distance from the camera, not size: `foreground` is nearest and most prominent, low in the frame; `midground` sits in the middle band, further back; `background` is furthest and smallest. The same element is drawn larger in the foreground than it would be deeper in the frame — but a size stated for an element always wins over its depth: a small object in the foreground is drawn close and sharp at its true size against the figures near it, never enlarged to fill the lower half. An element with no stated size that is genuinely large — a vessel, a building, a vehicle, a big animal — does dominate the foreground.

**COUNTS:** An exact number the scene states for a group of like things is three or fewer, and exactly that many are drawn. A group given as more than three, a cluster, a row, a few or several is drawn with no countable exact number.

**NO MARKS ON A CHARACTER:** No arrow, symbol, logo, badge, decal, sticker or coloured graphic is painted onto a character's skin, hair, face or clothing. A garment's own pattern and any emblem the Visual Bible states for that character are the only exceptions; nothing is added to mark, label or point at a figure, least of all on the back of a head.

**HANDS:** A character's hands hold only what the scene names for that character. **SHOT:** The scene description declares the shot. A close-up ends at the waist: legs, knees and feet lie below the bottom frame edge and cannot appear — never widen a close-up into a full-figure or establishing shot. A medium shot keeps each figure whole inside the frame. A wide shot shows the full setting. An ultra-wide shot shows the whole setting from a distance, the figures small within it and both ends of any separation visible.

**THIS IMAGE DEPICTS:** The group stops near the stone fountain in a strong wind as a raven swoops down and snatches the dry leaves from the open jacket, exposing the egg.

Generate a SINGLE illustration filling the canvas, bleeding off all four edges — no borders, frames, margins, white edges, panel keylines, split screens, grids, or collages. No lettering on any surface — no words, names or letters anywhere in the image. The only exception: text the Visual Bible explicitly specifies for an element is painted exactly as specified. Bracketed names like `[CharacterA]` and object ids are identifiers only — never painted into the image. Draw exactly one of each named object.

REFERENCE CARD COLOURS (each character's reference card has a coloured frame — match each person to their card):
- GREEN frame = Levin
- RED frame = Julian
- PURPLE frame = Max
- BLUE frame = Kiaan
The frame colours are identifiers ONLY. Never paint a coloured frame, border, or these colours onto any character, clothing, prop, or surface in the scene.

**WORN ITEMS ON THIS PAGE (the attached references are not authoritative for these):**
- Levin IS wearing this on this page: red wool cap — a chunky-knit red wool pull-on cap with a folded ribbed cuff. Draw it on Levin even if the attached reference shows Levin without it.
- Levin is NOT wearing this on this page: green fleece jacket — a forest-green zip-up fleece jacket with a wide body and two front pockets. Leave it off Levin even if the attached reference shows it worn — held open in his hands.
- Julian IS wearing this on this page: rust wool scarf — a long chunky rust-orange wool rectangular scarf in a plain knit. Draw it on Julian even if the attached reference shows Julian without it.

At the grey stone fountain, the four boys stop mid-stride in the sharp autumn wind while the raven strikes. Levin, in his red cap, white shirt, navy trousers, and brown boots, holds the open green fleece jacket out like a sagging cradle with both hands; inside it the greyish-white egg lies bare. Julian, in his sky-blue pullover, rust scarf, grey dungarees, and yellow boots, stands just behind Levin watching, while Kiaan, in his purple sweater, brown chinos, and dark grey sneakers, and Max, in his orange gilet over a grey shirt, blue jeans, and white sneakers, crowd close with Nia the terrier mix beside Max. The plump black raven flares its wings over the jacket, its blunted beak clamped around a large clump of dry yellow leaves, tugging them free as the wind whips more leaves across the gravel.
**REQUIRED OBJECTS IN THIS SCENE (each appears exactly as the scene description places it):**
* **dragon egg** (object) — about as big as a human head, like a lantern or a football — smooth, greyish-white oval shell
* **Nia** (animal) — stands knee-high to an adult
* **Raven** (animal) — about as big as a human head, like a lantern or a football
* **red cap** (clothing) (worn by Levin) — worn on Levin, not a separate free-standing copy
* **green fleece** (clothing) — held open in his hands
* **rust scarf** (clothing) (worn by Julian) — worn on Julian, not a separate free-standing copy
The attached reference images include rough images of: dragon egg; Nia; Raven — match each one's look at the size and placement the scene description gives it.
A state that divides, opens or breaks an object does not multiply its markings: a device, emblem or pattern on the surface is one marking, and the split runs through it — each part shows only its share.

**SEASON:** Autumn. Foliage, ground cover, sky and daylight colour are autumn's throughout the book — identical from page to page for the same place, and matching autumn even when a reference photo was taken in another season. Indoor frames and the page's own time of day are unaffected.

**ART STYLE:** A bold, expressive traditional watercolor painting: prominent visible brushstrokes, strong wet-on-wet washes bleeding together, pigment pooling and granulating, rough cold-press paper texture throughout, edges dissolving into the paper. Paint-dominant: no hard outlines, no ink or pencil lines. Characters stay fully opaque, never see-through. Warm, not overly vibrant. Painted by hand, never captured by a camera: no bokeh, no lens flare, no photographic grain, no skin pores, no camera-real fabric; depth from atmospheric haze, not optical blur; visible brushwork on every surface, faces included. No sharp photoreal rendering; a photograph with a painterly filter is still a photograph. Faces: loose washes with visible brushstroke texture. Each character keeps their real age — babies, children, teenagers, adults and grandparents each look it.

**REQUIRED CAST:** Every character named in the reference list is in the frame, exactly one of each, and no one else is added. A character the scene description gives no action to is still drawn, placed where the moment puts them and doing something consistent with it.

**DEPTH AND SIZE:** Depth is distance from the camera, not size: `foreground` is nearest and most prominent, low in the frame; `midground` sits in the middle band, further back; `background` is furthest and smallest. The same element is drawn larger in the foreground than it would be deeper in the frame — but a size stated for an element always wins over its depth: a small object in the foreground is drawn close and sharp at its true size against the figures near it, never enlarged to fill the lower half. An element with no stated size that is genuinely large — a vessel, a building, a vehicle, a big animal — does dominate the foreground.

**COUNTS:** An exact number the scene states for a group of like things is three or fewer, and exactly that many are drawn. A group given as more than three, a cluster, a row, a few or several is drawn with no countable exact number.

**NO MARKS ON A CHARACTER:** No arrow, symbol, logo, badge, decal, sticker or coloured graphic is painted onto a character's skin, hair, face or clothing. A garment's own pattern and any emblem the Visual Bible states for that character are the only exceptions; nothing is added to mark, label or point at a figure, least of all on the back of a head.

**HANDS:** A character's hands hold only what the scene names for that character. Never substitute an unnamed prop for a named one, and never fill an empty hand with an invented object — a hand with nothing assigned to it rests or gestures, and never joins a contact the scene gives to another part of that character's body.

**SHOT:** The scene description declares the shot. A close-up ends at the waist: legs, knees and feet lie below the bottom frame edge and cannot appear — never widen a close-up into a full-figure or establishing shot. A medium shot keeps each figure whole inside the frame. A wide shot shows the full setting. An ultra-wide shot shows the whole setting from a distance, the figures small within it and both ends of any separation visible.

EXACT POSES:
- Raven: tears the dry leaf bedding from the open jacket held open by Levin — green fleece
- Levin, Julian, Kiaan, Max: looking off into the scene, not at the viewer

EXPRESSIONS AND EYES (each face shows exactly this — no default smiles; each pair of eyes on exactly what is named):
- Levin: eyes wide in shock, mouth open in alarm; eyes on Raven
- Julian: brows pulled up in fear, lips parted; eyes on Raven
- Kiaan: eyes squeezed narrow against the wind, mouth tense; eyes on Raven
- Max: jaw dropped, eyes wide; eyes on Raven
